title: Coding Agents Don't Scale Themselves. Neither Do Your Teams. — Patrick Debois, Tessl
talk_summary: Debois argues agent adoption is an organizational/system problem: teams should stop hand-fixing agent output and instead improve reusable context, harnesses, planning, and platform ownership. He recommends measuring human touches and cost visibility, splitting well-scoped work to agents, and using risk-based auditing/verifiers for autonomy.

takeaways.what_they_do: Create a central catalog of reusable context, skills, and harnesses with an owner who makes them testable, extensible, and security-scanned; teams adopt paved roads instead of forking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Reusable context across teams. Why we all inventing how we do the authentication system, right? This is a shared component. Let's put it in the registry.

takeaways.what_they_do: Make token/iteration cost visible to the teams so they optimize model choice, context, and harness rather than just capping spend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if they visualize the cost, they might be eager to do some optimization in there, right?

takeaways.what_they_do: Split planning into sufficiently scoped items that can go straight to agents and ambiguous items that remain conversational human decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: things who were uh that were sufficiently scoped enough were easy to pick up by agents because they were well defined

takeaways.technique: Retro on system failures, not code fixes
takeaways.what_they_do: Use retros to identify repeated agent failures and fix the harness/context/tooling system instead of repeatedly patching individual outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent went over and over hit this problem. Can we fix the system?

takeaways.what_they_do: Not all features should be autonomous; invest in auditing, provenance, and verifiers, and choose autonomy level by risk.
takeaways.evidence_quote: invest more in auditing like provenence like who changed the code verifiers that kind of check whether that code was useful

takeaways.what_they_do: Measure how many human interventions are still needed for an agent to do the right thing; the number should fall as context and harness improve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start measuring how many human touches you still do to have the agent do the right thing
